input.question: If I traveled to space in a space ship that remained completely stationary, would I age faster than those on earth?
input.ground_truth: Due to special relativity, "completely stationary" doesn't make sense. In your reference frame, you would be stationary, so you would age faster. To someone on Earth, the planet would be stationary, so people on Earth would age faster.

Question: If I traveled to space in a space ship that remained completely stationary, would I age faster than those on earth?

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you and your friend are both 5 years old. You get into a super special spaceship that doesn’t move at all—it just stays in the same spot in space, like you’re standing still.

Now, your friend stays on Earth, playing and growing every day.

Here’s what happens:

On Earth, time goes at a normal speed. Your friend grows a little bit every year.

In your spaceship, if you are not moving at all (not spinning, not going fast), you are just sitting still in space. But space is a little bit different from Earth because of something called **gravity**. On Earth, gravity is strong, but in space, it is much weaker if you are far away from any big planet or star.

Because of this, time can actually go a tiny bit faster for you in space compared to someone on Earth. But it’s only a tiny, tiny bit—like if you waited 100 years, you would only be a *teeny* bit older than your friend on Earth. It’s so small, you wouldn’t even notice unless you waited hundreds of years!

So, you wouldn’t age *much* faster than your friend on Earth, but according to science, you might age just a *teensy* bit faster because of how gravity works. But it’s not like you’ll suddenly become a grown-up while your friend is still a kid!
